# Spatial discretization {#sec-ch04}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274 (chengcli/snapy, code_pin.yml)
sources: OUTLINE.md 4
status: draft

This chapter is the semi-discrete operator of one Runge–Kutta stage: everything that turns a cell-averaged
state into a tendency, and nothing that advances it in time. A stage reconstructs the primitive variables to
the faces, solves a Riemann problem on each face to get one flux there, makes that flux single-valued across a
process seam, takes its divergence, and adds the part of the curvature that is not a flux difference. Time
integration belongs to @sec-ch07, the well-balanced treatment of the vertical to @sec-ch05, and the positivity
limiter that runs between the Riemann solve and the divergence to @sec-ch08.

Acronyms used throughout: PLM[^rg-06abdc5ecbfb], piecewise-linear method; PPM[^rg-fee67a3928b8], piecewise-parabolic method; WENO[^rg-e22f686fce5d], weighted
essentially non-oscillatory; LMARS[^rg-f1575f33f70a], low-Mach approximate Riemann solver; HLLC[^rg-a10d6377330b], Harten–Lax–van Leer with the contact
restored; LLF[^rg-bf0815e12002], local Lax–Friedrichs; PVRS[^rg-9560824895ca], primitive-variable Riemann solver, the linear-acoustics pressure estimate of
@sec-ch04-hllc; TVD[^rg-bcc444f8446c], total-variation diminishing; MC[^rg-35c3aec5d6d0], the monotonised-central limiter.

Section 4A is the operator and its interchangeable parts: the divergence, the reconstruction framework with its
interpolants, the Riemann framework with its six solvers, seam averaging and the placement of the geometric
sources, whose derivation lives with the grids in @sec-ch03. Section 4B is one idea applied three times: an
average of a nonlinear expression is not that expression of the averages, and in a stratified column the two
differ at second order in $x_1$[^rg-11adc59a54dd]. The expression is a face flux for the first two sections and the
equation of state for the third. The algebra of every Derivation layer is checked with sympy in
`src/snapy_report/ch04/checks/derivation_check.py`, 19 of 19 claims passing.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch04-deps
#| fig-cap: "The dependency map of this chapter. A solid black arrow reads requires, a dashed green arrow reads implies. The reconstruction framework implies a pair of interpolants, and selecting either WENO type implies the matching linear polynomial for the velocity and pressure rows. The geometric sources require a solver that returns a face pressure, which three of the six provide. The horizontal covariance requires the geometric source to read the same shifted pressure, and the $x_1$ correction acts on the reconstructed velocity. Every edge is stated and cited in the section it comes from."
#| fig-alt: "Ten labelled boxes joined by arrows, with solid arrows for requires and dashed green arrows for implies, and a legend below."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch04.figures.fig_ch04_deps import make_fig
make_fig()
```

| scheme | switch | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Finite-volume update (@sec-ch04-divergence) | `disable-flux-x1\|x2\|x3` | all on | exact in flux form | `test_cubed_sphere_cell_volume_python` |
| Reconstruction framework (@sec-ch04-framework) | `reconstruct/{type,scale,shock}` | sub-block of the direction present: `dc`, false, false; absent: `dc`, false, true | set by the interpolant | `test_plm` |
| Donor cell (@sec-ch04-dc) | `type: dc` | the default type | 1 | `test_plm` |
| PLM (@sec-ch04-plm) | `type: plm` | off | 2, 1 at an extremum | `test_plm` |
| Centred cp3, cp5 (@sec-ch04-cp) | `type: cp3`, `cp5` | off | 3, 5 | `test_weno` |
| WENO3[^rg-3932dce05489], WENO5[^rg-4f39d4ebe8f7] (@sec-ch04-weno) | `type: weno3`, `weno5`; `scale`[^rg-7d2149f881dd] | off | 3, 5; weno3 is 2 at a critical point | `test_weno` |
| PPM (@sec-ch04-ppm) | `type: ppm` | off | none: the first stage throws | none |
| Radial $x_1$ volume coordinate (@sec-ch04-x1volume) | none; curved grid with `weno5` or `cp5` in $x_1$ | automatic | 5 at the faces, against 2 without it | `test_radial_order_python` |
| Riemann framework (@sec-ch04-riemann) | `riemann-solver/{type,dir}` | see @sec-ch04-riemann | — | `test_riemann` |
| LMARS (@sec-ch04-lmars) | `type: lmars` | off | acoustic face state, upwind transport | `test_riemann` |
| HLLC (@sec-ch04-hllc) | `type: hllc` | see @sec-ch04-riemann | three waves, exact contact | `test_riemann` |
| Roe (@sec-ch04-roe) | `type: roe` | see @sec-ch04-riemann | linearised, LLF fallback, no entropy fix | `test_riemann` |
| Shallow-water and plume Roe (@sec-ch04-shallow) | `type: shallow-roe`, `plume-roe` | off | plume-roe is Lax–Friedrichs | none in the default build |
| Seam averaging (@sec-ch04-seam) | none; split $x_1$ axis | automatic | restores telescoping | `test_x1_seam_split_mp` |
| Spherical-polar source placement (@sec-ch04-sphsrc) | none; coordinate type | automatic | three pressure branches | `test_coordinate` |
| Gnomonic source and frame placement (@sec-ch04-gnomonic) | none; coordinate type | automatic | rest to $10^{-14}$ | `test_hydrostatic` |
| Horizontal flux covariance (@sec-ch04-fluxcov) | `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE` | **on** | removes two $O(\Delta x_1^2)$ terms | `test_flux_covariance_rows_python` |
| $x_1$ mass covariance (@sec-ch04-x1masscov) | `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` | off | stored velocity 2 becomes 4 | `test_x1_seam_split_x1_mass_covariance` |
| Fourth-order $x_1$ conversion (@sec-ch04-conv4) | `dynamics/conversion-order` | 2 | 4 in $x_1$ against 2; $x_2$, $x_3$ stay 2 | `test_conversion_order_python` |

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-06abdc5ecbfb]: PLM — piecewise-linear method

[^rg-fee67a3928b8]: PPM — piecewise-parabolic method

[^rg-e22f686fce5d]: WENO — weighted essentially non-oscillatory

[^rg-f1575f33f70a]: LMARS — low-Mach approximate Riemann solver

[^rg-a10d6377330b]: HLLC — Harten–Lax–van Leer solver with the contact restored

[^rg-bf0815e12002]: LLF — local Lax–Friedrichs

[^rg-9560824895ca]: PVRS — primitive-variable Riemann solver

[^rg-bcc444f8446c]: TVD — total-variation diminishing; notation only; see @sec-appa

[^rg-35c3aec5d6d0]: MC — monotonised-central limiter

[^rg-11adc59a54dd]: $x_1, x_2, x_3$ — the three coordinate directions; $x_1$ is always the vertical (radial) direction

[^rg-3932dce05489]: WENO3 — third-order weighted essentially non-oscillatory reconstruction

[^rg-4f39d4ebe8f7]: WENO5 — fifth-order weighted essentially non-oscillatory reconstruction

[^rg-7d2149f881dd]: scale — scaling in the enclosing component: a reconstruction switch or values of a thermal-transport profile

[^rg-22d5fbfb3b96]: CPU — central processing unit

[^rg-81c093bded00]: CUDA — NVIDIA's parallel computing platform
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
